critical_code_review_comments: crisis_commander.py::run_regulatory_clock_alerts — dedupe key is a single 'alert_state' string ('approaching'|'overdue'). If a deadline is moved further out (via PATCH) after an 'approaching' alert fires, the state is not reset, so the alert will not re-fire when the new deadline approaches again. Consider resetting alert_state to '' inside the obligation PATCH handler when deadline_at changes.

crisis_commander.py::ingest_servicenow — 502 branches leak upstream status code but not the ServiceNow reason body; consider including r.text[:200] in the detail (redacted) to aid operators debugging a broken connection without needing server logs.

crisis_commander.py::email_crisis_brief — sends emails sequentially in a for-loop with await; for orgs with many admins this serialises Resend latency. Use asyncio.gather with per-recipient try/except to parallelise, keeping the same sent counter.

scheduled.py::hourly_overdue_digest — background_tasks.add_task(run_regulatory_clock_alerts) is called with no org_id → runs GLOBALLY across all tenants. Correct for a platform cron, but the audit trail from run_regulatory_clock_alerts only writes crisis_events per obligation; consider a single top-level audit row summarising 'cron: X orgs, Y alerts_sent' for observability.

crisis_commander.py::run_regulatory_clock_alerts uses db.crisis_obligations.find() streaming while calling update_one and insert_one inside the loop — safe with Motor async cursor, but be mindful that a very large obligation table + slow Slack/Teams webhook could hold the cursor open past MongoDB's default cursor timeout (10 min). Consider .to_list(500) or a bounded batch.
